newsitem.title: LUXEMBOURG: Cargolux to seek more seafood contacts.
newsitem.headline: Cargolux to seek more seafood contacts.

text.p: Cargolux said it would be at the European Seafood Exhibition to be held in Brussels betwee April 13 and 15.

"This will be our first appearance at the exhibition and as a worldwide transporter of seafood products we see it as an excellent opportunity to make contact with prospective clients," a Cargolux official told Reuters.
One of the main centres of origin of the fish and seafood freight transported by the Luxembourg-based cargo airline is Keflavik in Iceland.
Cargolux operates a weekly Boeing 747-200F westbound stopover in Keflavik en route to New York-JFK and also a weekly eastbound stopover from the U.S. to Luxembourg.

"On the westbound route, we are probably loading close to 20 tonnes of fish and seafood per flight , most of which is destined for fish markets in the Boston area," a Keflavik-based Cargolux official told Reuters.
He added:" Some of this volume is also made up of sea urchins destined for Japan via transhipment in New York."
On the eastbound route, Icelandic catches are destined for European markets and also for Asia, notably Singapore and Hong Kong, via Cargolux' 747F services from Luxembourg, the official said.
"Cargolux also carries fish and seafood orginating from Africa - Namibia - South Africa, Kenya and Uganda while its recently launched service from Santiago in Chile is another source of supplies."
The European Seafood Exhibition takes place in Brussels between April 15 and 17.
Cargolux operates a fleet of three Boeing 747-400Fs and is to take delivery of a further two 400Fs later this year.
It also operates four Boeing 747-200Fs, including one on leaseback. --Reuters Air Cargo Newsroom Tel+44 171 542-7706 Fax+5017
